title: Set full timing info for all navigation requests
body: A fetch controller's full timing info was only set when the request's destination was "document". HTML extracts it for every navigation that has a fetch controller, including those of iframe and frame elements, whose requests have the destination "iframe" and "frame". Those navigations hit the assert in extract full timing info. Setting it for every navigation request fixes that, and also makes it available for object and embed requests (see https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/13285). Found while reviewing https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/12890. - [x] At least two implementers are interested (and none opposed): * Not needed: browsers already expose navigation timing for iframe and frame navigations; this makes the specification match. - [x] [Tests](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt) are written and can be reviewed and commented upon at: * Covered by existing tests, such as [navigation-timing/nav2-test-navigate-iframe.html](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/blob/master/navigation-timing/nav2-test-navigate-iframe.html). - [x] [Implementation bugs](https://github.com/whatwg/meta/blob/main/MAINTAINERS.md#handling-pull-requests) are filed: * Not needed, see above. - [x] [MDN issue](https://github.com/whatwg/meta/blob/main/MAINTAINERS.md#handling-pull-requests) is filed: not needed. - [x] The top of this comment includes a [clear commit message](https://github.com/whatwg/meta/blob/main/COMMITTING.md) to use. (See [WHATWG Working Mode: Changes](https://whatwg.org/working-mode#changes) for more details.) *** Preview | Diff
